A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VIRTUE/SCaR research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original VIRTUE evaluations on MMEB and SCaR, component ablations, hyperparameter studies, and qualitative retrieval and correction results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds prompt-robustness experiments, further ablations, annotation-agreement statistics, and inference-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The proposed SAM-2/VLM architecture, convolution-plus-MLP connector, embedding concatenation, InfoNCE objective, and training procedure remain unchanged. Newly tested connector alternatives and SAM-2 finetuning are ablation variants, not changes to the adopted method.

E1.justification: The 36 MMEB tasks and five SCaR datasets remain unchanged. Section 5.4 extends evaluated input conditions to jittered, partially masked, and shifted visual prompts, centroid points, and random bounding boxes.

E2.justification: The main benchmark comparator sets in Tables 2–3 are unchanged. Appendix E.1 newly evaluates cross-attention and attention-pooling connector alternatives against Conv-MLP in Table 9, providing a limited expansion of comparison methods.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends the evaluation design with controlled prompt perturbations, substitutions, inference-only versus training-and-inference point removal, and SAM-2 freezing/finetuning comparisons. Appendix E.6 adds latency and memory measurements using batch size one on a single H100, with matched bf16 precision for I2T. Existing benchmark splits and primary training settings are retained.

E4.justification: Section 5.4 adds systematic robustness and prompt-dependence tests absent from v1. Appendix E.1 adds connector and SAM-2 finetuning ablations, while Appendices D.4 and E.6 add annotation-reliability and efficiency analyses. These materially expand scrutiny of component necessity, robustness, and practical cost.

E5.justification: v1 describes two independent inspectors without quantifying agreement. v2 first reports average Cohen’s kappa of 0.89 in Table 7 for that inspection process. Neither version reports performance uncertainty across repeated training runs.

E6.justification: The original benchmark scores are retained, but substantial new results appear. Table 4 reports random-box SCaR scores of 9.2 and 13.0 versus 27.8 and 56.9 with correct boxes; Table 5 reports a 68.6-to-24.1 MMEB drop when uniform points are removed only at inference. Tables 7, 9, and 11 add agreement, ablation, and efficiency results.

T1.justification: The formal retrieval task, representation definitions, connector equation, and InfoNCE objective are unchanged. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs that are added or revised in v2.

C1.justification: The introduction adds systematic analysis of visual-prompt integration and resulting guidance as an explicit contribution. The central VIRTUE and SCaR novelty claims and the abstract/conclusion performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that SCaR finetuning increases bounding-box dependence, random prompts demonstrate meaningful prompt use, and finetuning SAM-2 on uniform-point inputs biases it toward noninteractive settings. It also discusses accuracy–latency tradeoffs. The existing limitations and broader applicability discussion remain intact.

D1.justification: v2 replaces future-release and supplementary-material statements with explicit repository/project links and stated availability of code, models, and SCaR material. It also specifies 64 queries for attention pooling and hardware, precision, and batch size for profiling. Core training configurations are unchanged; external availability was not independently verified.

R1.justification: v2 adds You Mostly Walk Alone (Makansi et al., 2022) and ShuttleSHAP (Wang et al., 2025) to motivate prompt-dependence tests. The related-work discussion and principal research positioning otherwise remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section ordering are retained. Changes include local introduction edits, a clarifying task-instruction footnote, acknowledgements and publication-header updates, and insertion of Sections 5.4 and E.6. This is a localized expansion rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds a three-panel robustness figure and tables for prompt substitutions, point removal, annotator agreement, and efficiency. The ablation display expands from seven to nine panels. Several existing diagrams are redrawn, and retained qualitative figures are resized and relocated, substantially expanding the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked systematic tests of imperfect or irrelevant user prompts and an inference-cost assessment. Section 5.4 and Appendices E.1/E.6 add controls that test actual prompt dependence, justify design choices, and expose accuracy–cost tradeoffs. Appendix D.4 also quantifies annotation reliability. Together these substantially strengthen validation of the central interactive-embedding claim and assessment of its practical usefulness, while preserving the original benchmark evidence.
